stack.label: 02 / Stack
stack.caption: Components become skills
stack.title: A connected system, not a progress bar.
stack.intro: Select a technology to see what it’s for, what it connects to, and where it has shipped.

d.ts: The contract layer. Typed props, stores and API boundaries keep large codebases refactorable.
d.js: The runtime underneath everything — and knowing where it gets expensive.
d.html: Semantic structure and modern CSS. Layout, motion and accessibility start here.
d.vue: Primary framework. Composition API, composables and component design that scales across teams.
d.nuxt: Primary meta-framework. Hybrid rendering, layers and modules for products that need speed, SEO and structure.
d.react: Second home. Hooks, server components and the patterns that transfer between ecosystems.
d.next: App Router, streaming and server-first data for React products.
d.tw: Utility-first styling backed by design tokens, so themes and systems stay consistent.
d.arch: Boundaries, state ownership, rendering strategy and performance budgets — the decisions that outlive components.
